questions.question: Which one of the following is a component of Food Security System?
questions.solution:
• Buffer stock is a component of the Food Security System.
 
• It is the central stock maintained by the Government of India for various purposes of food security, such as taking care of emergency situations.
 
• Emergency situations can be crop failure or stabilization of prices by way of market intervention.

questions.question: What is the accepted average Calorie requirement for rural area in India?
questions.solution: In 1973, the poverty line was decided to be set as per nutritional intake of the citizens of India. The required amount of calories required for a person in rural area was set at 2400 and for urban at 2100 calories per day.

questions.question: Whose resolution is mandatory to impeach the President of India from his ofﬁce before the completion of his/her term?

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Either of the two houses of the parliament

questions.solution: The process of impeachment of President can start in either of the two houses of the Parliament i.e. Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. A resolution to impeach the President has to be passed by a two-third majority of the total number of members of the house where impeachment process had begun.

questions.question: How many types of writs are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **5 Writz**__ in the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as; Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 
 

 __Article__
 __Consists of__
 
 

 Article 32
 
 
Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of fundamental rights including the writs.

 __
 
• habeas corpus
 
• mandamus
 
• prohibition
 
• certiorari
 
• quo warranto
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Habeas Corpus: This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
• Mandamus: The writ of command is issued by supreme or high court when any government, court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty but fails to do so.
 
• Prohibition: It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent them from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• Certiorari: The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme or high court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
 
• Quo-Warranto: The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking of by what authority or warrant. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

questions.question: Who has built the Vijay Stambha (tower of victory) in Chittorgarh?
questions.solution: The Vijaya Stambha is a victory monument which is located inside the premises of Chittorgarh fort in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan. The tower was constructed by the Mewar king, Rana Kumbha, in 1448 to commemorate his victory over the armies of Malwa and Gujarat led by Mahmud Khilji.

questions.question: Who raised the slogan “Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it”?
questions.solution: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indian social reformer and freedom fighter, he was popularly known as ‘Lokamanya’. He adopted the slogan, “Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it” which was originally said in Marathi.

questions.question: Which Indian state is the largest in terms of the total area covered?
questions.solution: Rajasthan is India's largest state by area with a total surface area of 342,239 square kilometres which makes 10.4% of India's total area.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the longest Coastline?
questions.solution: Gujarat has the longest coastline in India with a total coastline length of 1214.7 km. The total coastline length of India is 7516.6 kilometres.

questions.question: Auxiliary bud develops into which of the following part of the plant?
questions.solution: The axillary bud is a shoot developed at embryo stage that is located in the axil (the space between the leaf and the branch) of a plant. Each bud has the potential to form shoots, and may be specialized in producing either vegetative or reproductive shoots.

questions.question: Xylem primarily transports which of the following?
questions.solution: Xylem is a transport tissue in vascular plants. Its primary function is to transport water from roots to shoots and leaves. But it also transports Nutrients

questions.question: Who proposed ﬁve kingdom classiﬁcation?
questions.solution: R.H. Whittaker was the first to propose the five-kingdom classification of the world's flora and fauna into the Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, Protista and Monera in 1969.

questions.question: What is the other name of Galileo's law of inertia?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e. __**Newton's ﬁrst law of motion**__.

__
 
• The other name of Galileo's law of inertia is **Newton's ﬁrst law of motion**__.
 
• Sir Isaac Newton first presented his three laws of motion in **1686**.
 
• His first law states that every object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change its state by the action of an external force.
 
• This concept is generally known as inertia.

**Extra information:**

 
• Newton’s First Law of motion- As per the newton’s first law of motion, if any object is in motion, then it will be continuously in motion, if it is in rest then it will be in rest, till any external force is not applied on it. It is also called the law of inertia.
 
• Newton’s Second Law of Motion- The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.
 
• Newton’s Third Law of motion- It describes that every action will have an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following device is best suited for measuring the temperature inside metallurgical furnaces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pyrometer. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• **Pyrometers are the temperature measuring devices** used to **detect the object’s temperature** and **electromagnetic radiation emitted** from the object.
 
• **Principle of Working :**
 
 
• It **measures the object’s temperature** by **sensing the heat/radiation emitted** from the object **without making contact with the object.**
 
 
 
• It **records the temperature level **depending upon the** intensity of radiation emitted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 

 
• **The pyrometer has two basic components** like **optical system and detectors** that are** used to measure the surface temperature of the object. **
 
• It is an** example of non- contact measurement.**
 
• **Thermocouple is a temperature-measuring** device** consisting of two wires of different metals joined at each end, **and works on **Seebeck effect.**
 
• **Thermometer **is also an** instrument **for **measuring temperature.**
 
• A **thermistor (or thermal resistor)** is defined as a** type of resistor **whose **electrical resistance varies** with **changes in temperature. **

questions.question: What is the full form of 'LAN'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Local Area Network (LAN):**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• It is a **computer network within a small geographical area**.
 
• A LAN is composed of interconnected workstations and personal computers which are each capable of accessing and sharing data and devices, such as printers, scanners and data storage devices, anywhere on the LAN.

questions.question: Which acid is released when an Ant bites?
questions.solution: Formic acid is released when an Ant bites. It is also called methanoic acid and is the simplest form of carboxylic acid.

questions.question: Which among the following is an example of solid sol?
questions.solution: Coloured gemstones are solid sol. These are the minerals in crystallised form that are used to make jewellery after rigorous polishing. There are certain coloured gemstones that are not the minerals such as jet, pearl and amber.

questions.question: Which metal is responsible for Itai-Itai disease?
questions.solution: Itai Itai, which literally translates to ‘it hurts, it hurts’ is the name given to cadmium poisoning. The name was given after the mass poisoning that happened in 1912 in Japanese town. Cadmium poisoning is characterised by softening of bones, kidney failure and unbearable pain.

questions.question: 'Vikalp' is a scheme launched by Indian Railways to help wait-listed passengers. Which of the following is NOT true about this scheme?

options.text: No-extra charges will be taken from passengers.
Wait-listed passengers can avail opportunity of travelling in Rajdhani/Shatabdi/Special trains even when booking made is in other mail/express trains.
Vikalp scheme will be initially available for e-tickets only.

questions.solution: Under the new reservation scheme called 'Vikalp', passengers who have booked tickets in other mail or express trains, can avail the option of travelling in premium trains to their booked destinations with no extra cost. This scheme was rolled out from 1st April, 2017.

questions.question: Who discovered the Cholera causing germ?
questions.solution:
• Filippo Pacini was an Italian anatomist, who became famous after his death for isolating the cholera bacillus Vibrio cholera in 1854.

Please note:

 
• In **1883, **Robert Koch identified the **vibrion for the second time**, after **Filippo Pacini’s discovery in 1854.**

questions.question: 'Hunar Haat' an exhibition to exhibit and promote the arts and artisans from minority community was launched at which of the following events?

options.text: Indian International Trade Fair, New Delhi, 2016

questions.solution: The Hunar Haat exhibition was organised at Indian International Trade Fair in 2016 in which around 184 artisans from all over the country exhibited their skill in various art forms.

questions.question: Which movie won the award for the best movie at the Oscar Awards 2017?
questions.solution: Moonlight won the Academy Award (Oscar) for best movie of 2016. La La Land is a 2016 American musical romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Damien Chazelle.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book titled 'Citizen and Society'?
questions.solution: Hamid Ansari, former Vice-president of India, is the author of the book titled ‘Citizen and society’. He served the office for two terms from 2007-2017.

questions.question: With which country India has recently signed a MoU for Water Conservation in India?
questions.solution: India signed a MoU with Israel in June, 2017 for Water conservation. In July, 2017 Narendra Modi became the first Indian Prime Minister to visit Israel.

questions.question: Which among the following neighbouring country of India is the largest producer of Opium in the World?
questions.solution: Afghanistan is the largest producer of the opium in the world followed by Myanmar, Mexico and India.
